body.statement:
The literal coordinatewise no-wider requirement has a finite-sample valid
fallback. In the spectral-split calibration handle, take the measurable
covariance envelope to be the constant function \(K_\Sigma\), and define
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal C}_n^M(\alpha)=\mathcal C_n^M(\alpha),
 \qquad
 \widetilde{\mathcal R}_n=\mathcal R_n,
 \qquad
 \widetilde{\mathcal C}_n^h=\mathcal C_n^h.
\]
Then every coordinate interval is no wider than its deterministic
\(K_\Sigma\)-box counterpart with probability one, the moment region has
finite-sample coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) uniformly over the compact
class, and the rational encoding and exact semialgebraic inverse are
preserved. This construction certifies equality of widths; the frozen
handle is not used here to claim a strict adaptive improvement.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\geq3\) and a data-generating law \(P\) in the compact stable class. Equip the trajectory space
\(\Omega_n=\mathbb R^{(n+1)d}\) with its Borel \(\sigma\)-field and define
\[
 \widehat K_{\Sigma,n}:\Omega_n\longrightarrow(0,\infty),
 \qquad
 \widehat K_{\Sigma,n}(w):=K_\Sigma.
\]
This constant map is measurable: for each Borel set \(E\subseteq(0,\infty)\), its inverse image is \(\Omega_n\) if \(K_\Sigma\in E\), and is empty otherwise.

Let \(\Sigma_{n,P}:=\operatorname{Cov}_P(W_n)\). The coarse spectral-density resolvent bound in
\(\mathrm{thm{:}uniform\mbox{-}moment\mbox{-}box}\), applied with the restrictions collected in \(\mathrm{def{:}compact\mbox{-}class}\), gives
\[
 0\preceq\Sigma_{n,P}\preceq K_\Sigma I_{(n+1)d},
 \qquad
 \|\Sigma_{n,P}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq K_\Sigma
 =\widehat K_{\Sigma,n}(W_n)
 \quad P\text{-almost surely}.
\]
Thus the proposed envelope dominates the trajectory covariance simultaneously over the compact class at every finite sample size.

To check its compatibility with the spectral-split handle, fix a symmetric lag-moment matrix \(H_{\ell ij}\) from \(\mathrm{Hell}\), and write its spectral decomposition as
\(H_{\ell ij}=H_{\ell ij}^{+}-H_{\ell ij}^{-}\), where
\(H_{\ell ij}^{+}\succeq0\) and \(H_{\ell ij}^{-}\succeq0\). For either \(s\in\{+,-\}\), covariance domination and congruence by \((H_{\ell ij}^{s})^{1/2}\) give
\[
 \operatorname{tr}(H_{\ell ij}^{s}\Sigma_{n,P})
 =\operatorname{tr}\!\left((H_{\ell ij}^{s})^{1/2}
 \Sigma_{n,P}(H_{\ell ij}^{s})^{1/2}\right)
 \leq K_\Sigma\operatorname{tr}(H_{\ell ij}^{s}).
\]
Submultiplicativity of the operator norm also gives
\[
 \bigl\|\Sigma_{n,P}^{1/2}H_{\ell ij}^{s}
 \Sigma_{n,P}^{1/2}\bigr\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq\|\Sigma_{n,P}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \|H_{\ell ij}^{s}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq K_\Sigma\|H_{\ell ij}^{s}\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
Hence both spectral parts are controlled by the measurable constant envelope. Recombining the two parts recovers the same deterministic two-sided calibration already certified by
\(\mathrm{thm{:}uniform\mbox{-}moment\mbox{-}box}\).

Define, for every realized trajectory,
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal C}_n^M(\alpha):=\mathcal C_n^M(\alpha),
 \qquad
 \widetilde{\mathcal R}_n:=\mathcal R_n,
 \qquad
 \widetilde{\mathcal C}_n^h:=\mathcal C_n^h.
\]
For each \((\ell,i,j)\in\{0,1\}\times V\times V\), the coordinate interval of the first set is therefore exactly
\[
 \operatorname{Out}_N\!\left((\widehat M_\ell)_{ij},
 2K_\Sigma\left\{
 \sqrt{\frac{\log(4d^2/\alpha)}{n}}
 +\frac{\log(4d^2/\alpha)}{n}\right\}\right),
\]
which is the corresponding deterministic-\(K_\Sigma\) interval in
\(\mathrm{def{:}moment\mbox{-}box}\). The widths are consequently equal for every sample point, so
\[
 P\!\left\{\text{all fallback coordinate widths are no larger than
 their deterministic-\(K_\Sigma\) counterparts}\right\}=1.
\]

The equality of the two moment regions and
\(\mathrm{thm{:}uniform\mbox{-}moment\mbox{-}box}\) imply
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cmp}}}
 P\{(M_0,M_1)\in\widetilde{\mathcal C}_n^M(\alpha)\}
 =
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cmp}}}
 P\{(M_0,M_1)\in\mathcal C_n^M(\alpha)\}
 \geq1-\alpha,
\]
where \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cmp}}\) denotes the fixed compact class of
\(\mathrm{def{:}compact\mbox{-}class}\). Each coordinate endpoint is rational by the defining guarantee of \(\operatorname{Out}_N\). Finally,
\(\widetilde{\mathcal R}_n=\mathcal R_n\) leaves every polynomial equality and inequality in \(\mathrm{def{:}inverse\mbox{-}region}\) unchanged, while
\(\widetilde{\mathcal C}_n^h=\mathcal C_n^h\) leaves its transfer projection unchanged. Thus the rational encoding and exact branch-free semialgebraic inversion are preserved. By \(\mathrm{thm{:}global\mbox{-}honest\mbox{-}inversion}\), the same equalities also retain finite-sample transfer coverage. All comparisons are equalities, so the proof makes no claim of strict adaptive improvement.
